I vote Sims 3. I read through everything that EA took out of Sims 4 that was in 3 and didn't want anything to do with 4. Sure there's advanced emotions or whatever in 4, but no more living world? Really? It's like playing the Sims 1 all over again. That's my biggest gripe for 4.
I played both non-seriously and I kind of prefer 4 due to the increased customization for people and homes. Granted, I just build homes and move onto the next house without playing too much.

The sims 4 was a complete waste of money on account of the fact the game is CONSTANTLY reminding you that there is DLC you can buy. You don't need any of it, its mostly just cosmetic, but it is like getting bashed in the face with a newspaper ad every time I did something in it.

I'll preface by saying that I've never played Sims 4, but I was heavily interested in the Sims 4 controversy so I read a lot about it.

Sims 4 rips out a ton of content. I think they've gone back and added in pools but I'm not sure about toddlers, which I always felt was a huge part of the gameplay.

Sims 3 has a cool, open map where you can just zoom out from your house and click anywhere on that map, and your Sim will go there. This opens up a lot of possibilities and means drastically less loading times. You can go shopping for food, studying books, etc., go to the movies or out on dates, go fishing, and so on.

But like any Sims title, you need all of the expansions (and a healthy dose of mods, too) to make the game really enjoyable and unlock its full potential. And that's where Sims 4 falls way short.

Sims 2 gives you more to do than Sims 3, but Sims 3 eliminates the ridiculous loading time. Sims 3 is prettier, the mods are prettier and more diverse. There's a TON to do. Sims 4 wiped all of that out.

The only negative about Sims 3 is that a lot of people have issues running it, usually due to lag and the shitty programming. There are mods that may or may not fix the issues. I know the biggest one I ran into a LOT was corrupt saves. But I've still sunk hundreds of hours into that game because it's so much fun and customizable.

You can change the colors and patterns on your clothing, floors, walls, objects, etc., and that was one of my favorite things about Sims 3. Sims 4 ripped that out, and it's not going to be implemented in the future, last I heard.

Captain Beefheart and His Magic Band - Safe As Milk (1999 CD Version)

This is Buddah Records' remastered reissue of The Magic Band's 1967 debut album, Safe as Milk. The reissue was released in 1999, containing the original 12 tracks, as well as 7 bonus tracks that were originally intended for the unreleased "Brown Wrapper" follow-up album. The bonus tracks were recorded about 2 months after the original release of Safe as Milk, as well as from the same sessions used to record the songs for the 1971 album "Mirror Man".

While more conventional and accessible than Beefheart's later work, Safe As Milk is still an incredible album that introduced the bluesy, idiosyncratic, and experimental groundwork that would be expanded upon in The Magic Band's later work such as Trout Mask Replica. The non-replicable sound of the band can most easily be heard in Electricity, through the Captain's raw, sour vocals, the constantly-changing tempo, and Samuel Hoffman's fitting use of the theremin.
